proof:
# Exact failure of the actual own-depth capacity principle

This counterexample concerns the proposed capacity built from actual
own-fiber halfspace depths. It does not refute OC: capacity is a lower bound
on cap volume, and that lower bound can be too small even when the required
mixed-volume center exists.

## 1. Definitions

For a planar convex body K and x in K, let

    f_K(x)=inf{|K intersect H|: H is a closed planar halfspace containing x},
    A(K)=max_(x in K) f_K(x).

For a finite positive fiber family S, define

    nu(H)=sum_z sup_(x in K_z, (z,x) in H) f_(K_z)(x),     (1)

with empty suprema equal to zero. This is exactly the proposed capacity
with g(z,x)=f_(K_z)(x)^(1/2), since g^2=f. Every term in (1) is at most
the area of its fiber cap, so nu(H)<=mu(S intersect H).

The proposed principle at the three-point base {-1,0,1}, whose Helly number
is two, would assert maximum capacity depth at least sum_z A(K_z)/2.
The construction below has maximum capacity depth strictly smaller.

## 2. A constrained own-depth maximum in a simplex vertex cap

Let T be a planar triangle of area c, with centroid g and a vertex v.
For 0<k<=2/3 let H be the vertex-side halfplane cutting off the triangle

    T intersect H = v+k(T-v).

Then

    sup_(x in T intersect H) f_T(x)=c k^2.               (2)

The upper bound is immediate: H itself is a containing halfspace for every
candidate in that cap. For the lower bound, the larger homothetic triangle

    L=v+(3k/2)(T-v)

is contained in T. Its centroid q=v+(3k/2)(g-v) lies on the cap boundary,
at that boundary segment's midpoint. Classical continuous Grunbaum at
the centroid of a triangle gives, for every halfspace G containing q,

    |T intersect G|>=|L intersect G|>=(4/9)|L|=c k^2.

This proves (2). It only uses the ordinary triangle centroid theorem,
not any mixed-integer statement. Also A(T)=(4/9)c: the centroid gives
the lower bound, and one of the three centroid facet caps contains every
candidate and has area (4/9)c. Thus a halfplane containing g has constrained
own-depth maximum exactly (4/9)c.

## 3. The exact actual convex fibers

Use the same rational body as in `candidate 84ed2ea21a94e03a`:

    T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)},
    A=conv{(0,0),(4/5,0),(0,8/25)},
    eta=2^(-20), s=3/128+eta,
    K_-=(2-s)A, K_0=T, K_+=sA,
    C=conv(({−1} times K_-) union ({0} times T)
                                  union ({1} times K_+)).

The midpoint Minkowski sum of the endpoint fibers equals A, which lies in
T. Hence the actual integer fibers of C are exactly these three positive
triangles. The body is full-dimensional in R^3 and its only integer
projection indices are -1,0,1.

Write c=|T|=1/2, a=|K_-|, b=|K_+|, gamma=4/9, and

    e=(32/125)s^2,       delta=(128/125)eta.

Then

    b/c=e,    a/c=1+e-delta,    M/c=2+2e-delta.           (3)

In particular e>delta>0, as checked exactly by the companion verifier.
Thus a>c>b. All three own-depth peaks are

    A(K_-)=gamma a, A(T)=gamma c, A(K_+)=gamma b.

The proposed capacity threshold is gamma M/2, exceeding gamma a by

    gamma(M/2-a)=gamma c delta/2=1/9216000.               (4)

## 4. Three fixed bad caps cover the entire middle fiber

Set

    k=2/3-eta,       p=1/3+eta=1-k,
    h=13/40,        B=(8/25)(1-s).

Consider the closed ambient halfspaces

    H_A={y+Bz>=h},
    H_B={x+y-2z<=k},
    H_C={x+2z>=p}.                                      (5)

They cover every point of the middle fiber T. Indeed a point outside H_A
and H_C has y<h and x<p, whence x+y<p+h<k, so belongs to H_B. The strict
cover margin is k-p-h=1/120-2eta>0. Closed boundaries are included throughout.

For H_A the largest endpoint value of y+Bz is exactly 8/25 on each
endpoint fiber, which is smaller than h. Thus the endpoints are excluded.
The middle cap y>=h contains the middle centroid because h<1/3. Hence

    nu(H_A)=gamma c<gamma a.                             (6)

For H_B the entire left fiber is excluded: there x+y-2z=x+y+2>=2>k.
The entire right fiber is included, since its maximum x+y-2 is
(4/5)s-2<k. The middle cap x+y<=k is a vertex cap with ratio k.
Equation (2) gives

    nu(H_B)=c k^2+gamma b.                               (7)

For H_C the left fiber is again excluded: its maximum x+2z is
(4/5)(2-s)-2<p. The right fiber is included since its minimum x+2z is
2>p. The middle cap x>=p=1-k is another vertex cap of the same ratio.
Therefore

    nu(H_C)=c k^2+gamma b.                               (8)

Both these capacities are strictly below gamma a. In normalized units,

    [gamma a-(c k^2+gamma b)]/c
       =gamma(1-delta)-k^2
       =(988/1125)eta-eta^2>0.                           (9)

Equations (5)--(9) certify every point of the entire middle triangle,
not merely its centroid or a line of candidates.

## 5. The exact maximum capacity depth

Every point in the left fiber has the vertical isolating cap z<=-1, whose
capacity is gamma a. Every point in the right fiber has z>=1, whose
capacity is gamma b. The three preceding caps give a smaller capacity for
every point in the middle fiber. Thus maximum capacity depth is at most
gamma a.

Conversely take the actual centroid of the left triangle. Every containing
ambient halfspace contains this point in its left-fiber cap; the supremum
in (1) for that fiber is at least its own-depth value gamma a. Therefore

    max_(y in S) inf_(H contains y) nu(H)=gamma a
        <(A(K_-)+A(T)+A(K_+))/2.                         (10)

The strict deficit is exactly the number in (4). This disproves the special
actual own-depth capacity principle already for n=1,d=2, with positive
simplex fibers and rational data.

The own-depth root g in this example has the advertised joint concavity.
For any two fibers and points, the Minkowski sum of their like-oriented
through-point caps lies in the target through-point cap. Ordinary
Brunn--Minkowski, followed by the infimum over directions, proves the
pointwise square-root concavity on the actual convex family. Own-depth
also vanishes on each continuous fiber boundary. Thus neither those
properties nor the exact own-depth interpretation rescues the capacity
principle.

All arithmetic and halfspace incidence comparisons are verified exactly
in `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_actual_own_depth_capacity_counterexample.py`. The only ordinary
continuous input is the classical triangle centroid bound used in (2).
